Let me evaluate against the rubric.

C1: Introduction identifies three ethical issues, links to engineering design, discusses organisational context ("design-process decision made by the organisation"), and stakeholders with Table 1. Excellent — 10.

C2: Balanced discussion — arguments for and against with depth, conclusions with recommendations for multiple stakeholders (Rachel, management, health department, chip supplier, engineers). Excellent — 10.

C3: Compelling argument, logical structure, systematic understanding for all stakeholders. Very good to excellent. The structure is logical, arguments support conclusion well. I'd say 10 or 8. The arguments are compelling and conclusion well supported; systematic understanding for all stakeholders demonstrated. I'll give 10. Actually maybe 8 to be conservative? The report is quite strong. Arguments are compelling, supported by structure, conclusion well supported, systematic understanding for all stakeholders. Excellent — 10.

C4: Research and evidence — references [1]-[8], quantitative evidence (81 of 236 trusts, 19,000 appointments, $475M, $4.3B, 11 million vehicles), qualitative (Therac-25, Code of Ethics). Excellent — 10.

C5: Structure, format, language — abstract, intro, body, conclusion, recommendations; two tables and a figure; IEEE references; fluent writing. Excellent — 10. Minor: heading levels inconsistent (OCR artefact possibly). Word count unknown but seems within limit. Give 10.

Requirements:
R1: yes — scenario analysed, physical harm vs data loss distinction addressed.
R2: yes — "shipping on the current basis is not an ethical way to conduct business" and decision rule.
R3: yes — trade-offs in Table 2 and arguments (time, competitive pressure, revenue, employment, large-scale testing).
R4: yes — health department contract, WannaCry, hospitals, emergency services.
R5: yes — stakeholders table, arguments for/against.
R6: yes — references, case studies, not just legal compliance.
R7: yes — recommendations section.

Technical issues: minor — WannaCry case is a cyberattack not hardware defect (student acknowledges this). Intel $475M figure correct. VW $4.3B correct. Stalk 1988 correct. No real technical errors. Maybe note the figure's decision rule is sound. One minor: "at least 81 of 236 hospital trusts" — NAO reported 81 trusts affected out of 236; correct.

Overall: excellent report.
